summary.headline: Suprajit Q4 FY26: quarterly revenue crossed INR 1,000 crore, Q4 consolidated PBT ~INR 97 crore (almost double YoY); FY27 guide: double-digit growth, consolidated EBITDA margin 12-13.5%.
summary.overview: Management reported that Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue crossed INR 1,000 crore on a quarterly run rate, with consolidated PBT of about INR 97 crore, almost double last year. Full-year revenue grew about 17% and EBITDA about 19-20%, helped by the SCS (ex-SES) turnaround, which turned EBITDA positive in Q4 at about +2% after roughly -20% in Q1. Standalone and ex-SCS growth was more modest (standalone revenue +7.1%, ex-SCS consolidated revenue +8.7%). Management guided to double-digit FY27 revenue growth and a 12-13.5% consolidated EBITDA margin, with GCM (including SCS) margins rising from about 6% to 10-12%.

financial_highlights.metric: Consolidated operational EBITDA, FY26 (ex-SCS basis as stated)
Surplus cash in mutual funds, March 2026

segments.name: SCD (Suprajit Controls Division, to be renamed GCM)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew about 10% and EBITDA margin crossed double digits for the first time at 11% for FY26. Mexico consolidated into Matamoros and Brownsville made main US warehouse; SAL India and Shanghai Lone Star each grew about 20%.

segments.name: DCD (Domestic Cable Division, to be renamed ICM)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew about 9%, dampened by YoY price concessions passed to customers; management says EBITDA margin was robust and unchanged for the year. Margin optics were weighed by STC and corporate overheads being allocated to DCD.

segments.name: PLD (Phoenix Lamps, to be renamed PLE)
segments.commentary: Revenue fell about 3% and EBITDA declined as commodity (moly, tungsten) increases were not fully passed on; margin down about 200 bps, with TRIFA brand sales hit by Middle East conflict. First orders executed for a large US retailer.

segments.name: SED (Suprajit Electronics Division, to be renamed for sensors, electronics and displays)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew about 20-30% (figures cited differently on the call) with EBITDA growing substantially; management expects double-digit margin in FY27 (about 10% currently). Digital clusters and electronic throttle controls driving momentum.

segments.name: SCS (Suprajit Components/SES, Europe and Morocco business)
segments.commentary: Turned EBITDA positive in Q4 (about +2%) after -20% in Q1, -6% in Q2 and -2% in Q3. Poland shut, manufacturing moved to Morocco (single shift), warehouse moved from Germany to Hungary, and tool room moved to Morocco; SCS will be folded into GCM from Q1 FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 group revenue: double-digit growth expected.
FY27 consolidated EBITDA margin guided at 12% to 13.5%, inclusive of SCS.
GCM (SCD plus SCS): double-digit revenue growth; EBITDA margin expected to rise to 10-12% from about 6% in FY26.
ICM (India cables): double-digit revenue growth with stable EBITDA margin, citing market share gains, Beyond Cable ramp-ups, and insolvency of a large European halogen lamp maker.
FY27 capex about INR 200 crore: about INR 80 crore India, about INR 50 crore global, about INR 50 crore STC, about INR 15-16 crore corporate.
Margin guidance excludes the approximately $6 million Section 301 tariff recovery claim, which is pending in court; management expects it within 3-6 months if resolved.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex about INR 200 crore: land and building about INR 80 crore, plant and machinery about INR 105 crore, software and IT about INR 15 crore.

Electronics Division central building to be demolished and rebuilt as a three-storey facility over two years (about INR 30-40 crore total, about half in FY27); operations relocated to leased premises meanwhile.
SAL Chennai Plant-2 (Vallam) to be built for SAL captive capacity; SCD capacity expansion and SCD India Chennai expansion planned.
STC new building delayed, now expected to complete in Q3 FY27.
Morocco operating mainly on one shift, so management sees no capacity constraint there.
demand_pricing: Management attributes DCD revenue slowdown to YoY price cuts; underlying India volume growth said to be about 12-14% ex-PLD, ahead of industry (around 11% last year).

Pass-through: management expects most commodity cost increases to be recovered from customers; tariff recoveries from customers and US government ongoing, with US refund portal process causing timing lag.
Tariff leakage: unrecovered Mexico steel duties of about $1-2 million absorbed in FY26 P&L, expected to persist in material cost in FY27 and FY28.
Halogen lamp market: largest halogen lamp maker's insolvency is driving new low-cost sourcing enquiries to India; Indian OEMs with halogen tails already buying from PLD.

Electronics: throttles (ferrite-magnet based), digital clusters (Supra 1.0/2.0/2.5/3.0 platforms) and actuators (seat-lock, charging-gun) are new products; mostly two-wheeler today, with a North American off-highway cluster win starting this year.
China: supplying a large Chinese EV OEM with door lock and latch cables; around 20+ projects, 3-4 commercialised; management aspires to about 20% share of that customer's business in 2-3 years.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 margin guidance at risk from Middle East-driven cost inflation, and what gives confidence on growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth confidence rests on already-won business that executes a year later; launch delays are the main risk. Management expects most commodity increases to be passed to customers and calls the forecast conservative.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin dip in last two halves: is it tariff under-recovery?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman said some tariff recoveries are yet to happen and may be skewing the number; he would check the H1 vs H2 gross margin split. Management said unrecovered tariffs are charged off, so any recovery is upside.

qa_highlights.question: Break-up of INR 200 crore capex by division and Electronics Division allocation?
qa_highlights.answer: India about INR 80 crore, global about INR 50 crore, STC about INR 50 crore, corporate about INR 15-16 crore; Electronics building is INR 30-40 crore over two years.

qa_highlights.question: Why are DCD and Phoenix Lamps margins down, and what recovers them?
qa_highlights.answer: DCD margin is strong; the drop reflects STC (about 150 staff vs 50-60 a year earlier) and corporate SAP/global costs allocated to DCD. PLD margin fell about 200 bps on flat top line and TRIFA/aftermarket softness; recovery expected from a US retailer, Indian aftermarket and European insolvency-driven demand.

qa_highlights.question: Does the SCS/GCM margin jump from 6% to 10-12% come from tariff recovery or operations?
qa_highlights.answer: Mostly operational: restructuring at SCS and Controls, Juarez to Matamoros, Jiaxing stabilisation, and Europe relocation to Hungary/Morocco. Tariff recovery is a smaller contributor and the guidance excludes the $6 million Section 301 claim.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Mexico steel duty costs and the $6 million Section 301 claim affect FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Unrecovered Mexico duties of $1-2 million will be a permanent material cost. The $6 million Section 301 claim is excluded from guidance; resolution expected in 3-6 months.

risks_watch: Middle East conflict driving commodity and supply-chain cost inflation; recovery from customers is assumed but not assured.
Customer launch timing slips could delay the double-digit growth guidance.
Unrecovered Mexico steel tariffs of about $1-2 million a year become a permanent material cost.
Timing of US tariff refunds and the pending $6 million Section 301 recovery; both are court and portal dependent.
Phoenix Lamps margin recovery depends on the US retailer ramp and aftermarket revival; halogen tail declines slowly.
Electronics margin guidance is only for one year; FY28+ unclear.
Management declined to give a China share number explicitly; China aspiration of about 20% of one customer's business is unproven.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the SCS turnaround and FY27 margin path, but hedged repeatedly on Middle East, commodity and launch-timing risks. Evasive on quantifying the FY26 tariff charge, the Q3-Q4 gross margin dip and the order book; detailed on capex and division renaming.
key_quotes: So, we see much more consistency coming in the directional improvement. And now, we have to start moving up north much faster.
I think the heavy lifting of the significant restructuring is all behind us. Hence, the outlook is good.
Our margin guidance is without considering that, yes.

adds.what: STC new building (delayed, expected to complete Q3 FY27)
SAL Chennai Plant-2 (Vallam) for SAL captive capacity
SCD capacity expansion and SCD India Chennai expansion (for new business win)
Electronics Division central building rebuild as three-storey facility over two years (INR 30-40 cr total)

growth.why: Management guides double-digit FY27 group revenue growth and a 12-13.5% consolidated EBITDA margin, with capex of about INR 200 crore and SCD/SAL capacity expansions planned, but no specific capacity volumes or timelines beyond STC (Q3 FY27) are given; utilisation is described only as mostly one shift, and the SCS turnaround and ICM share gains are supportive but not quantified.
